From the upper-left cell to the lower-right cell, a side-to-side path needs at least 3 moves right and 4 moves down. Thus it must visit at least 8 distinct cells. The four dominoes cover exactly 8 cells, so the path uses them all and makes exactly those 7 moves, with no backtracking.

Conversely, any ordering of the 3 right moves and 4 down moves gives a path of 8 cells. Pair cells 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, and 7–8 to form the dominoes. This pairing is forced: nonconsecutive cells of a monotone path are never side-adjacent, so the first unpaired cell must pair with the next. The covered cells also determine their path order, since the distance from the starting cell increases by 1 at each move.

Thus arrangements correspond exactly to choices of the 3 right-move positions among 7, giving (7 × 6 × 5)/(3 × 2 × 1) = 35.
Final answer: 35
